sealed_batches.why_superseded: this batch is the batch that found the confound: with the covering element now named, the A arm's offline navigation is blocked by BUTTON.v8-primary-button (data-testid=plan-ai-submit, aria-disabled=true) inside DIV.v8-sheet-backdrop -- a plan-AI sheet my own walk left open. A modal sitting over the bottom bar is by design, so '0 of 3 destinations' would have described my leftover UI state and not the generation under test. The instrument now normalises that state before the outage and records it as a precondition; batch 4 is measured with it in place.
sealed_batches.instrument_change_after: added closeOpenSheet()/sheetState() before ctx.setOffline(true) on every P4 arm, phases.P4.precondition + ui_state_before_offline recorded, and the deriver treats a nav still covered at that moment as ARM_INVALID rather than as a product verdict

how_to_read_a_name: batch<N> tells the chronological attempt on this base; the suffix states what the INSTRUMENT of that batch could not record -- it is never a product finding. Each folder keeps its own SUPERSEDED.json whose readings_of_these_rounds were recomputed from those rounds' artifacts at seal time, so a retired round stays auditable.
